correctness.rationale: For any finite ordinary derivative measure, the exact signed-jump integral representation and Minkowski reduce the sharp norm to steps. Mehler reversibility gives R(s)=p-2E q_r+E q_{ru}. Differentiation yields q_r′(s)=-2 phi(s) Phi(-b_r s); b_{ru}^2=(b_r^2+b_u^2)/(1+b_r^2 b_u^2), and strict subadditivity of erf makes R′(s)<0 for s>0 when nu([0,1))>0. Reflection gives strict unique maximum s=0. Sheppard quadrant identity gives the exact formula and rigidity. Limit expansions are standard. The 101-check standalone checker independently quadratures finite examples; proof covers all laws and BV functions.

value.rationale: One sharp theorem handles all Borel positive Mehler mixtures, with a formula only involving one- and two-fold correlation averages and a complete equality classification. The median rigidity is structurally nontrivial because the squared residual contains competing positive and negative Gaussian correlation terms. The pure OU family yields exact all-time and short-time constants. These are reusable calibration results for regularization with randomized or subordinated Gaussian smoothing, beyond one numerical cutoff.
